title: Eskart: One Card for Eskişehir's Trams and Buses
excerpt: Eskişehir's Eskart pays on the ESTRAM trams and the city buses, with a 60-minute transfer window and an online top-up that only reaches the card when you tap it. Plus how to get here from Istanbul by YHT or coach, and the tram doors that won't open unless you press the button.
bodyHtml:
One card, the tram and the buses

Eskişehir's transport card is the Eskart. It is a brand of ESTRAM, the company that runs the city's trams, and the card applications themselves are handled by the Eskişehir Büyükşehir Belediyesi transport department. One card pays on the ESTRAM trams and on the city buses, and you can change between the two on the same card. It's a local card: ESTRAM's own FAQ says the Eskart works only in Eskişehir.

The tram network

ESTRAM opened on 24 December 2004 and has grown into a network of roughly 55 km. The current line diagram shows nine numbered lines. The main ones meet in the centre around the Belediye and ES-ES stops:

  • 1 Otogar – SSK, from the intercity bus terminal through the centre and past the railway station

  • 3 OGÜ – SSK, which also passes the railway station

  • 4 Otogar – OGÜ, and 36 Otogar – Opera – OGÜ

  • 7, 8 and 9, ring lines out to Çankaya, Batıkent and Çamlıca

  • 10 Şehir Hastanesi – Kumlubel, and 12 75. Yıl – OGÜ, out east through Emek and 71 Evler

According to ESTRAM, the first tram leaves the Otogar platform at around 05:15 and the last one runs back in just before 01:00. Since 16 May 2024 there have also been night trams on some lines; the lines and times are on the ESTRAM website. City bus timetables are on the municipality's website, and the Estram Mobil app shows trams and buses live.

Where to get one

A standard full-fare Eskart is sold at the municipality's kiosks (büfe) and at private dealers around the city. There's no application for it. Discounted and free-travel cards are a different matter: you apply for those at the Eskart Başvuru Merkezi at Köprübaşı Caddesi No: 9/2 in Çukurçarşı, open weekdays from 08:00 to 17:30. ESTRAM's FAQ says you can also make a first application online through its website.

Topping up

You can top up at Eskart top-up machines (they take banknotes; put the card in the green slot on the right and follow the screen), through the Estram Mobil app, or online through the Online EsKart Yükleme page on estram.com.tr, which takes a bank card with 3D Secure.

The online top-up trap. An app or website top-up is not written to the card straight away. The payment page says it becomes active in the system within 30 minutes, and it only moves onto the card the next time you tap the card on a tram or bus validator. Until then, the card itself still holds the old balance. If you're about to board with an empty card, use a machine.

The app

Estram Mobil (free on the App Store and Google Play) tops up and renews physical and virtual Eskarts, checks the balance by tapping the card on your phone or typing in its number, shows your recent boardings, and shows trams and buses live with a Nasıl Giderim route planner. It can also hold a virtual Eskart and pay by NFC or QR code, and it sells single QR tickets. A QR ticket is valid for 24 hours but includes no transfer, so on a day with changes it's the expensive option.

Transfers

The FAQ is clear about the rule. Within 60 minutes of boarding you can transfer tram to tram, tram to bus, bus to tram or bus to bus. The transfer isn't free: the official tariff charges a small transfer fee instead of a second full fare. Two exceptions: getting back on the same line or the same bus doesn't count as a transfer and is charged as a new boarding, and bank-card and QR-ticket rides get no transfer at all.

No card yet? Your bank card works

The official tariff includes a fare for contactless debit and credit cards. It costs a little more than an Eskart tap because the bank's service charge is added, and you get no transfers. It's fine for your first ride from the station. For a stay of any length, buy a real Eskart.

What a ride costs

Fares change often, so we don't quote them here. Before you load the card, check the current tariff on the ESTRAM or municipality pages linked below. One thing that's useful to know: buses out to the rural districts and villages are charged at two, three or four times the city fare, depending on the zone. Minibüs and dolmuş routes have their own fare, and the official pages don't say whether they take the Eskart, so don't count on it.

Card types and discounts

Besides the standard card, the municipality issues discounted cards to students, teachers and people aged 60 and over, and a free-travel serbest kart to people aged 65 and over. There are also separate cards for disabled people, veterans and a few other groups. Every application needs a recent passport photo and the original nüfus cüzdanı, the Turkish national ID card. The official pages don't mention foreign nationals at all. If you have a residence permit, take it with you to the Eskart Başvuru Merkezi and ask; whether you qualify is for them to decide.

Students at Eskişehir Osmangazi Üniversitesi and Eskişehir Teknik Üniversitesi don't need a separate card. Their university ID card works on the trams and buses once it has been registered at the Eskart Başvuru Merkezi. Students can also put a monthly student subscription (abonman) on the card through the app or at a top-up point. It gives unlimited rides for the cardholder only: if you tap it again on the same validator for a friend, that ride is charged at the full fare.

The yearly renewal trap. A discounted or free card is valid for one year from the date you applied, and then it has to be renewed (vize), online, in the app or at the centre. If you miss the renewal, the card can no longer be topped up and whatever balance is left is charged at the full fare. The same happens when your student or teacher status ends.

If you lose an ID-linked (kimlikli) Eskart, the centre can cancel it and issue a new one. The FAQ describes no such option for the anonymous card you buy at a kiosk, so treat the balance on that one like cash.

On the tram: three things that catch people out

  • The doors don't open by themselves. When the tram stops, the driver unlocks the doors, but only the doors where someone has pressed the button open. Press it to get off, and press it on the outside to get on.

  • Everyone over six needs a card and has to show it if asked. Riding without one counts as travelling without a ticket and is penalised under the Misdemeanours Law. Using someone else's personalised discount card can get the card confiscated.

  • Bikes and scooters only if folded, and backpacks should be carried in your hand. Pets are allowed only in a closed carrier, and guide dogs are welcome.

Getting here from Istanbul: the YHT

The fastest way in is TCDD's YHT high-speed train. The dedicated Eskişehir – İstanbul YHT starts and ends at Söğütlüçeşme on the Asian side and also stops at Bostancı and Pendik, then calls at Gebze, İzmit, Arifiye, Bilecik and Bozüyük on the way. The Ankara – İstanbul YHTs also stop at Eskişehir, and they carry on past Söğütlüçeşme to Bakırköy and Halkalı on the European side, which is handy if you live there. Not every train stops at every station; TCDD notes, for example, that the early-morning express YHTs between Ankara and Istanbul only pick up at Eskişehir and Pendik. Expect a journey of roughly three hours from Söğütlüçeşme, but check the time for the train you book on TCDD's timetable, because it varies by departure.

Eskişehir's railway station is on the tram network. Its tram stop is Ulus Anıtı (Gar), served by lines 1 and 3, so you can step off the train and onto a tram, using a bank card if you don't have an Eskart yet.

Getting here by coach: the otogar

Intercity coaches arrive at the Otogar, the city's bus terminal. It has its own tram platform and is the end of lines 1, 4 and 36, so no taxi is needed. Line 1 runs through the centre and past the railway station, and lines 4 and 36 run to the OGÜ end of the network.
